title: Microsoft Purview: network data security with Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access)
summary: Hold: the Graph call uses a version that does not document the security-profile session control, and two configuration paths omit required selections. The claim that inspection requires a Conditional Access assignment also overlooks the baseline security profile. The rollout, opt-in default and licence combinations are supported.

claims.claim: Purview network data security integrates with Microsoft Entra Internet Access through Global Secure Access.
claims.quote: Extend Microsoft Purview data security controls to the network layer by integrating with Entra Internet Access.

claims.claim: The integration inspects text, prompts and files from managed devices sent to AI apps and other internet destinations.
claims.quote: These controls apply to content shared from managed endpoints through browsers, applications, add-ins, APIs, and more.

claims.claim: Global Secure Access Administrator configures Global Secure Access settings.
claims.quote: A user with the Global Secure Access Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID to configure Global Secure Access settings.

Browse to Identity > Protection > Conditional Access.
Select + Create new policy.
Under Session, select Use Global Secure Access Security Profile and select the security profile you created.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies is the automation equivalent for assigning a Global Secure Access security profile to groups.
claims.quote: globalSecureAccessFilteringProfile | globalSecureAccessFilteringProfileSessionControl | Session control to link to Global Secure Access security profiles or filtering profiles.
claims.fix: Use POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-post-policies?view=graph-rest-beta. Replace the row note and the final paragraph's portal-only qualification with: 'Graph beta: conditions.users.includeGroups supplies the group IDs; sessionControls.globalSecureAccessFilteringProfile sets isEnabled to true and profileId to the security profile ID. Beta APIs are subject to change and not supported for production use.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/conditionalaccesssessioncontrols?view=graph-rest-beta, https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/globalsecureaccessfilteringprofilesessioncontrol?view=graph-rest-beta and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/conditionalaccessusers?view=graph-rest-beta. The v1.0 sessionControls reference has no globalSecureAccessFilteringProfile property.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: Scan with Purview needs both halves
claims.claim: Scan with Purview needs a matching Purview DLP policy targeting inline web traffic to inspect content or enforce audit and block decisions.
claims.quote: Without a matching Purview DLP policy, the content policy can't inspect selected file or text content or enforce audit or block decisions.

claims.claim: Network data security supports the Audit only action.
claims.quote: Network data security supports Audit only and Block actions.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Network data security supports blocking the matching activity.
claims.quote: Global Secure Access forwards matching upload traffic to Microsoft Purview for content inspection. Purview evaluates the content against your DLP policy and returns a decision based on your DLP rule action. Global Secure Access then enforces the result.

claims.claim: Sensitive information types can be used as policy conditions for network inspection.
claims.quote:
Under Conditions
1. Select + Add condition then choose Content contains.
2. Select Add and choose Sensitive info types.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can be used as network inspection policy conditions.
claims.quote:
Using this, you can audit and block selected file and text content based on conditions such as:

claims.claim: The user's risk level can be a condition for Scan with Purview audit and block decisions.
claims.quote:
Using this, you can audit and block selected file and text content based on conditions such as:
- Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels
- Sensitive content in files or text
- The user's risk level

claims.claim: Unmanaged cloud app data sources come from the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps catalogue.
claims.quote: Unmanaged cloud apps - Network data security collection policies support all the sources that are in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Cloud app catalog which includes over 35,000 discoverable cloud apps.

claims.quote: In scenarios where Purview inspection is unable to complete, such as a payload that is too large to inspect, or an internal error, the traffic is allowed (fail-open).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who is covered
claims.claim: Scan with Purview inspects only traffic mapped to an Entra user identity.
claims.quote: Scan with Purview only applies to traffic associated with an Entra user identity. Traffic that cannot be mapped to an Entra user identity is not sent to Purview for inspection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who is covered
claims.claim: Purview network data security policies do not apply to B2B guests.
claims.quote: Purview network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: A policy targeting an unmanaged app can capture consumer and enterprise interactions sharing the app URL.
claims.quote: Policies that target unmanaged apps can capture interactions from both the consumer and enterprise versions of an app when the app's URL is shared across instances (for example, ChatGPT consumer and ChatGPT enterprise).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Who is covered; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Only users assigned a security profile through Conditional Access can have traffic inspected.
claims.quote: The baseline security profile applies to all traffic even without linking it to a Conditional Access policy. It enforces policy at the lowest priority in the policy stack, applying to all Internet Access traffic routed through the service as a 'catch-all' policy.
claims.fix: Narrow these statements to the documented Conditional Access deployment rather than claiming exclusivity. Replace the risk bullet with 'For the Conditional Access deployment described here, review the security-profile assignment when checking pilot coverage.' Replace Scope's opening sentence with 'The deployment described here targets users whose traffic is routed through Global Secure Access Internet Access and whose Conditional Access policy applies the configured security profile.' Replace the impact rationale with 'Medium. Users in the configured pilot group can see uploads and prompts to AI and cloud apps blocked.' Remove 'Only users assigned ... have traffic inspected'; the general security-profile documentation also describes a baseline profile without a Conditional Access link.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Blocking HTML or JSON content types can unintentionally block normal web and API traffic.
claims.quote: Web requests and responses commonly use HTML or JSON payloads, so blocking these text types can unintentionally block normal web and API traffic, including GET, POST, and PUT operations.

claims.claim: Exceeding GSA API rate limits blocks traffic fail-closed.
claims.quote: Requests are subject to API rate limiting based on usage. When limits are exceeded, traffic is automatically blocked (fail-closed).

claims.claim: The Session type condition can scope a content rule to AI agent traffic.
claims.quote: Configure the Session type condition to scope the rule by traffic origin. Select Agent to match traffic classified as AI agent traffic.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A TLS inspection policy is a prerequisite.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Internet Access traffic forwarding profile must be enabled.
claims.quote: Enable the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile and ensure correct user assignments.

claims.claim: The GSA client requires an Entra ID joined or hybrid joined device.
claims.quote: The Global Secure Access client requires a device (or virtual machine) that is either Microsoft Entra ID joined or Microsoft Entra ID Hybrid joined.

claims.claim: QUIC over UDP is not supported.
claims.quote: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) traffic (that is, QUIC) isn't supported.

claims.claim: The content-filtering setup lists GSA clients on Windows and macOS.
claims.quote: Install the Global Secure Access client on Windows or macOS.

claims.claim: Policy distribution to the network security solution can take up to 24 hours.
claims.quote: allow up to 24 hours for your policies to be distributed to the network security solution and for the first data to show up.

claims.claim: After the services communicate, request data can take up to 30 minutes to appear in the audit log and activity explorer.
claims.quote: Once the two services fully communicate with each other, it can take up to 30 minutes for data about a request from a client to a website or cloud app to appear in the audit log and activity explorer.

claims.claim: The GSA content-policy prerequisites list a valid Entra Internet Access licence.
claims.quote: A valid Microsoft Entra Internet Access license.

claims.claim: The GSA content-policy prerequisites require a valid Purview licence for Scan with Purview.
claims.quote: A valid Microsoft Purview license, required for Scan with Purview inspection.

claims.claim: Basic content filtering can be used without a Purview licence.
claims.quote: You can use basic content filtering without a Purview license.

claims.claim: Non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser integrations require Purview E5 or equivalent together with pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote:
Network data security with non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser solutions requires:
- Purview E5 (or equivalent) per-seat licenses and the Microsoft Purview pay-as-you-go billing model.

claims.claim: The non-Microsoft integration pay-as-you-go unit is a request, meaning each device or browser network call to a website or API.
claims.quote: Network data security uses the request as unit of measure for pay-as-you-go billing purposes when using non-Microsoft SASE and secure browser integrations. A request is each network call made from a device or browser to a website or API.

claims.claim: Prices are on the licensing pages linked from the network data security article.
claims.quote: Searched: "aka.ms/M365EnterprisePlans" "price"; "Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans" "prices". Read the linked Security service description and platform pricing excerpts; no passage verifies prices on those specific links.
claims.fix: Replace 'Prices are on the licensing pages Learn links from the network data security page' with 'For enterprise plan pricing, see Compare Microsoft 365 Enterprise plans: https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/compare-microsoft-365-enterprise-plans.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/office-365-platform-service-description#microsoft-365-and-office-365-plans, which explicitly directs readers there for pricing.

claims.claim: Learn names DLP Compliance Management and Information Protection Admin as example roles for accessing Data loss prevention.
claims.quote: If you don't see Data loss prevention in Microsoft Purview, your account might not have the required permissions or your tenant might not have the required licensing. You need a role such as DLP Compliance Management or Information Protection Admin

claims.claim: Network content filtering supports only the Internet Access profile.
claims.quote: Network content filtering is supported with the Internet access profile only

claims.claim: Including all catalogue entries for an app with multiple entries avoids coverage gaps.
claims.quote: When multiple catalog entries exist for the same app with differences in the entry name (for example, QwenAI and Qwen Chat), include all entries for the app to avoid unintended coverage gaps.

claims.claim: The network DLP policy can first run in simulation mode.
claims.quote: On the Policy mode page, choose Turn the policy on immediately or run in simulation mode first to test.

claims.claim: Purview rule actions should match the activities and content types selected in the GSA content rule.
claims.quote: The actions you select in the Purview DLP rule should match the content types and activities you selected in the Global Secure Access content policy.

claims.claim: DLP alerts can be reviewed in the Purview portal at Data loss prevention > Alerts.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
To review DLP alerts and their associated events, go to Data loss prevention > Alerts.

claims.claim: Activity explorer can be filtered for Network DLP activities.
claims.quote: To investigate matching activities, open Activity explorer and filter for Network DLP activities or the policy, user, or app you want to review.

claims.claim: For GSA content rules, Purview alerts and Activity explorer apply only when Scan with Purview is used.
claims.quote: Purview alerts and Activity explorer apply only when you use Scan with Purview.

claims.claim: Basic Allow and Block content rules are investigated through GSA traffic logs instead.
claims.quote: If you use basic content policy with Allow or Block actions, review the Global Secure Access traffic logs instead.

claims.claim: The path that links a content policy to a security profile ends at Global Secure Access > Secure > Security profiles > the profile > Link policies.
claims.quote:
Switch to the Link policies view.
Configure the link content policy:
1. Select + Link a policy > Existing Content policy.
2. From the Policy name menu, select the content policy you created.
claims.fix: Replace the parenthetical route with 'Global Secure Access > Secure > Security profiles > profile > Link policies > + Link a policy > Existing Content policy > Policy name > content policy'. The original stops at a view before the selections that choose a content-policy link.

claims.claim: Collection policies provide network data discovery rather than DLP enforcement.
claims.quote: extending discovery and protection to the network layer through collection policies for data discovery, data loss prevention policies for protection, or both

claims.claim: The network data security article lists activity explorer, DSPM activity explorer events and DLP alerts as investigation destinations.
claims.quote: Data from network data security appear in activity explorer, Data Security Posture Management activity explorer events, and if alerts are enabled, DLP alerts.

claims.claim: The governance checklist names controls and monitoring surfaces that have no corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote:
Check ... the Internet Access forwarding profile, a TLS inspection policy ...
Review Data loss prevention > Alerts and Activity explorer ...
Query GSA traffic logs ...
The table has only DLP policy, content policy, and Conditional Access rows.
claims.fix: Checklist steps for checking the Internet Access forwarding profile and TLS inspection, linking a content policy to a security profile, reviewing DLP Alerts and Activity explorer, and querying GSA traffic logs have no corresponding table rows. This finding identifies the mismatch only; it does not request additional rows.
